evidence.correctness: Ran experiments/run.py: results.txt reproduced byte-identically (45 s). Recomputed lexicon-coder Wald/plus-two/Wilson coverage at k=5,10,20,50 by exact binomial enumeration with my own formulas: 0.641/0.857/0.900/0.926 for Wald against 0.628/0.853/0.917/0.936 reported, Wilson 0.951 vs 0.953 at k=5. Wilson(3/10) and Beta(3.5,7.5) quantiles recomputed by hand/numerical integration and match the test constants. Differences are within Monte Carlo error except k=20 (0.017, finite-population effect).
evidence.completeness: Everything the README says is done runs: run.py regenerates results.txt, figure.py regenerates the SVG, 4 unit tests pass, all 16 headline numbers match results.txt, README and project.json links valid, listed in research/README.md. Stated next steps (group gap, LLM coder) are honestly marked not done.
evidence.verification: python3 -m unittest test_qualnegint: 4 tests OK. Six hand-seeded mutations in qualnegint.py: 4 caught (Wilson variance, Z95, Jeffreys upper index, Wilson centre), 2 survived (plus_two n+2 -> n+1; strata_counts weight -> 0.5). The stratum weights behind every coverage number and the plus-two formula have no value test; run.py has no test.
evidence.craft: Read qualnegint.py (54 lines), test_qualnegint.py, run.py, figure.py. Small, stdlib-only, seeded, clear docstrings, shared linefig used. Defects: sys.path juggling with a module called 'run' (collision hit during audit), scipy cited but not a dependency, jeffreys returns an unused point estimate, no guard for n=0.
evidence.claims: All headline and table numbers match results.txt, 'not LLMs' disclosure is prominent, limits section is good (selection bias of worst-of-four, approximate Wilson, no FPC for Jeffreys). Two Results sentences are wrong against the table: Wald at k=50 is 0.6-2 points short not 2-4; Jeffreys range is 0.942-0.978 not 0.94-0.96. Minor, not the headline.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun and extend it, and a coder-validation practitioner learns 'use Wilson, not Wald, at k=5'. But that is the Brown-Cai-DasGupta (2001) lesson applied to one estimator; stratified/weighted-Wilson and survey-statistics prior work and the design-based supervised learning literature are not cited, one population and four miss-rate points are studied, and it is a single-session simulation rather than a PhD-level programme result.
evidence.domain: A survey statistician would ask for a design-based (FPC, weighted) Wilson as in Kott and Carr / Dean and Pagano, a sweep over true stratum proportions given coverage oscillation, Clopper-Pearson or exact stratified comparators, and the weighted-sum Jeffreys posterior justified. The README names its approximations honestly, but the method is a first-pass combination rather than established practice.

defects.what: Two seeded bugs survived all 4 tests: the plus-two shift (n+2 vs n+1) is only checked for being wider than Wald, and strata_counts (the stratum weights every coverage number depends on) has no test at all. Experiments/run.py has no test either; a wrong weight would change every headline number and pass CI.

Nearest prior work missing: the project's contribution is a stratified/weighted Wilson and Jeffreys interval, but only single-proportion references are given. Survey-statistics intervals for weighted proportions (Kott and Carr 1997; Dean and Pagano 2015), Agresti-Caffo, and design-based supervised learning (Egami et al. 2023), which solves the same 'validate an automated coder with few hand labels' problem, are absent, so the novelty of 'most of the undercoverage was the interval' is not placed. That small-n Wald fails and Wilson/Jeffreys fix it is the textbook result of Brown, Cai and DasGupta (2001).

Coverage is measured on one population with four coders, i.e. four (p_neg, p_pos) pairs; coverage of binomial intervals oscillates with p, so 'Wilson covers 94-95%' is not shown to hold for other miss rates or other prevalences. No finite-population correction (180 of 459 positives are sampled), so the conservative direction is not quantified; exact enumeration here gives Wald 0.900 against reported 0.917 at k=20.
Two sentences in Results misstate results.txt: Wald is 0.6-2.0 points short at k=50 (not 2-4); Jeffreys spans 0.942-0.978 across cells (not 0.94-0.96) and is not clearly more even than Wilson.

Fragile imports: run.py puts three directories on sys.path and imports the module named 'run' (qual-real's downloader); any other directory holding run.py first on the path breaks it with AttributeError (hit while auditing). Test comments cite scipy as the source of constants but scipy is not a project dependency (values do check out).

recommended_fixes: Add tests: strata_counts on a hand-built 4-item example (weights 0.75/0.25), plus_two value for [(1.0,3,10)] against the (4/12) Wald interval, and a single-stratum Jeffreys MC test already exists. Kills both surviving mutants.
Correct README lines about Wald at k=50 ('0.6-2 points short') and Jeffreys ('0.942-0.978').

Add the survey-statistics and design-based supervised-learning references and a paragraph placing the contribution; sweep p_neg/p_pos on a grid with exact enumeration (as in the audit script) to show coverage is not an artefact of four coders.
verdict: Sound, reproducible and honest small simulation study: the results file regenerates exactly and independent exact-binomial recomputation agrees with the reported coverage to within Monte Carlo error. It does not meet the bar because verification is 2: two of six seeded bugs, including the stratum weights behind every number, survive the tests. Beyond that, it is a textbook result (Wilson/Jeffreys beat Wald at small n) applied to one estimator with one population, missing the stratified-interval prior work, so fitness and domain are 2 and it is well short of the PhD-level research bar. Two Results sentences misquote the table.
